In Deutschland werden politische und wissenschaftliche Fragen durch einen engen Meinungskorridor gezwängt. Gedanken und Äußerungen, die nicht hindurchpassen, werden an Strafen geknüpft. Angefangen mit öffentlicher und sozialer Ächtung bis hin zur Inhaftierung. Diese Menschen haben niemandem etwas weggenommen, haben niemandem Gewalt angetan, haben niemanden verletzt oder beraubt. Sie haben lediglich ihren Mund aufgemacht oder kritische Fragen gestellt. Einer dieser Menschen ist Ursula Haferbeck. Am 7. Mai 2018 wurde die damals 90-jährige, international bekannte Dissidentin und Bürgerrechtlerin Ursula Haferbeck in ihrem Haus in Flothow festgenommen und in die JVA Bielefeld-Pragwede gebracht. Seitdem sitzt sie mittlerweile im geschlossenen Vollzug eine mehrjährige Haftstrafe wegen Meinungsdelikten ab. Mit einer baldigen Haftentlassung ist nicht zu rechnen. Seit der Inhaftierung vor einem Jahr gab es unzählige Solidaritätsaktionen in ganz Deutschland. Partei- und gruppenübergreifend werden die Proteste für die sofortige Freilassung von Ursula Haferbeck unterstützt. Zum 91. Geburtstag der inhaftierten Bürgerrechtlerin Ursula Haferbeck findet am 9. November in Bielefeld eine Demonstration statt, die mitten durch die Innenstadt zum Justizkomplex führt. Wie kann es sein, dass eine alte Dame für Worte inhaftiert wird? Die Frage ist Grund genug für uns alle, den Geburtstag angemessen zu begehen und ein Zeichen der Hoffnung, ein Zeichen der Solidarität zu senden. Kommt zur Geburtstagsdemonstration am 9. November 2019.

Angefangen mit öffentlicher und sozialer Ächtung bis hin zur Inhaftierung. Diese Menschen haben niemandem etwas weggenommen, haben niemandem Gewalt angetan, haben niemanden verletzt oder beraubt. Sie haben lediglich ihren Mund aufgemacht oder kritische Fragen gestellt. Einer dieser Menschen ist Ursula Haferbeck. Am 7. Mai 2018 wurde die damals 90-jährige, international bekannte Dissidentin und Bürgerrechtlerin Ursula Haferbeck in ihrem Haus in Flothow festgenommen und in die JVA Bielefeld-Pragwede gebracht. Seitdem sitzt sie mittlerweile im geschlossenen Vollzug eine mehrjährige Haftstrafe wegen Meinungsdelikten ab. Mit einer baldigen Haftentlassung ist nicht zu rechnen. November in Bielefeld eine Demonstration statt, die mitten durch die Innenstadt zum Justizkomplex führt. Wie kann es sein, dass eine alte Dame für Worte inhaftiert wird? Die Frage ist Grund genug für uns alle, den Geburtstag angemessen zu begehen und ein Zeichen der Hoffnung, ein Zeichen der Solidarität zu senden. Kommt zur Geburtstagsdemonstration am 9. November 2019.

Famed music producer and convicted murderer Phil Spector has died at the age of 81. The California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation revealed in a statement that Phil, who had been an inmate at the California Health Care Facility in Stockton, California since 2013, had passed away from natural causes. While it is currently unknown what caused Phil's death, the CDCR noted that its official cause of death will be determined by the medical examiner in the San Joaquin County Sheriff's Office. In the same statement, the CDCR also included an updated mugshot of Phil that was taken last November. Phil, who often wore wigs before his conviction, is seen bald and smiling in the recent mugshot. Back in 2009, Phil was found guilty of second-degree murder for the death of actress Lana Clarkson. This conviction happened in a second trial after the first one was deadlocked in 2007. Phil ended up being sentenced to 19 years to life in prison and was eligible for a parole hearing in 2025. Phil, who was born Harvey Phillips Spector in 1939, is known for revolutionizing rock and pop music in the 1960s with his layered wall of sound production technique. During his career, Phil has produced music for legendary bands and artists such as the Beatles, the Ramones, and even share.

Our moon. A strange thing, don't you think? Have you ever gazed upon a full moon and wondered, wondered how it got there, what strange forces could have possibly built it? There are many moons within our solar system, yet few are as strange as ours. No others are known to ring like a bell when struck. No others possess such luminosity as our moon. In the 1970s, Michael Vassin and Alexander Shashurbakov, of what was then the Soviet Academy of Sciences, created a thesis that the moon is actually the remnants of a very ancient spaceship created by, as yet, unknown civilization. The article was entitled, Is the Moon the Creation of Alien Intelligence?, and was published in Sputnik, the Soviet equivalent of Reader's Digest. The suggestion of a hollow moon first appeared in science fiction when H.G. Wells wrote about a hollow moon in his 1901 book, The First Men in the Moon. Michael Vassin and Alexander Shashurbakov's hypothesis is based on the fact that large lunar craters, generally assumed to be formed from massive meteor impacts, are generally too shallow for scars made upon an organic body, and can have flat or even convex bottoms. They proposed that small meteors are making cup-shaped depressions in the rocky surface of the moon, while the larger meteors are drilling through a rocky upper layer, hitting an armored hull underneath. Does George Lucas know something we don't? It seems he couldn't resist adding just one crater. The authors referenced earlier speculations by astrophysicist Iosef Shiklovsky, who suggested that the Martian moon Phobos was an artificial satellite and hollow. Interestingly, Phobos has been claimed to appear to be hollow by numerous astronomers, who have stated that it appears to have an opening on one side, making it, in a sense, similar in shape to an empty shell. Phobos's orbit is also a complete mystery. Many who have researched it claimed that it should have crashed into the surface of Mars many moons ago. Between 1972 and 1977, seismometers installed on our moon by the Apollo missions recorded strange moonquakes. The moon was described to have been ringing like a bell during some of those quakes. The supportive evidence was then brought to popular attention in March 1970, in an article in Popular Science. When Apollo 12 deliberately crashed the ascent stage of its lunar module into the moon's surface, it was claimed that the moon rang like a bell for an hour, leading to arguments that it must be hollow. Several YouTubers, most notably Crow777, have supposedly recorded what is now known as lunar waves, if confirmed to exist. This may prove there is some form of functioning shield or scanning system being seen working on its surface. The fact that the moon is less dense than the Earth is also strong supportive evidence that it is indeed hollow.

Whether it's questions about curriculum or incidents of anti-Semitism and hate, the ADL has helped us if we've missed the mark and mentored us and guided us. We mark today with a ceremony of remembrance, solidarity, and hope. Through the words of our tradition, with the guidance and love of several of our diverse Jewish community's spiritual leaders, may we draw strength and inspiration from those who've come before us as we invoke the guidance and presence of the divine. Fear cannot be the driver of our life. Instead, we need to lead with chesed, with love, with generosity, with compassion, resilience, and hope. And I think it is critically important that the federal government recognize the role that it plays and make sure, again, that that support is cascading down through various ways through which we can call attention to it and fund programs to combat it. So just because I want to talk about these issues, of course, it affected me and my family. But I remember what my mom told me when I was nine years old. He said, stand up for something, even if it means sacrifice and everything. And that's what I'm trying to do. The history between the NAACP and the ADL is critically important for us all to understand. The NAACP and the ADL have walked in lockstep in the pursuit of freedom for all people, the right of all of us to be self-determinative, and in the quest for the dignity of every human being. And so today, now more than ever, I believe that it is critically important for us to continue that legacy. We have to become the unwelcome guest at the dinner table. And not just for the young people at the table, but to telegraph the message that this is not acceptable. But I think that if anything good can come from this moment, it's for us to think about the fact that, you know, Jewish history is written in the present. We are writing our chapter of Jewish history. I thought that it was a very powerful experience, and I've been looking forward to this for a while. I'm probably going to go back to campus and continue to fight the fight against anti-Semitism and not back down and stay strong. Fighting anti-Semitism must be, it must be one of our priorities in the work to create justice, inclusivity, equity, safety, and security. So we are in this fight together. Thank you for being here. Thank you.
